title: Hybrid cache alignment and subword-aware quant kernel hinting
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Reduce dequantization overhead and SLO variance for mixed-precision (INT8/FP8) streaming decode by (a) aligning KV cache allocations and microbatch boundaries with quant tile sizes, and (b) introducing a lightweight kernel-hint metadata layer that drives head-level kernel selection based on token/subword characteristics and recent latency telemetry. This ticket captures the design, implementation plan, benchmarks, and rollout steps for the first-phase prototype.
technical_design:
Motivation:
Current hybrid INT8/FP8 paths incur frequent small dequant/cast operations when KV cache slices or microbatch boundaries do not match kernel-friendly tile sizes. Small dequant calls are expensive on some HW and create tail latency variance during decode. We also observe that token-level characteristics (e.g., short subwords vs long words, punctuation) correlate with attention head activation sparsity and per-head numerical range, which can influence whether INT8 or FP8 yields better latency/cost tradeoffs for that head at a given moment.

Proposed approach:
1) Cache alignment: modify KV cache allocator to expose a "quant tile alignment" option. When enabled, prefill allocations for new sequences round up to nearest tile multiple (configurable per-model: e.g., 128 or 256 elements) to ensure dequant and matmul kernels can operate on full tiles. This reduces amortized per-token dequant calls and increases contiguous memory throughput.

2) Subword-aware microbatching: extend request preprocessor to tag request tokens with subword-length feature and a rolling token-entropy heuristic. Microbatch joiner will prefer to aggregate tokens with similar subword profiles to avoid mixing tiny and large token vectors that force irregular kernel shapes. This provides more stable kernel invocation shapes and better batching efficiency.

3) Kernel-hint metadata: introduce a small per-layer, per-head hint that the serving runtime will read at dispatch time. Hints include preferred precision ("int8" | "fp8" | "auto"), expected activation magnitude bucket (low/med/high), and a fast-decay score from telemetry. Hints are advisory: kernel selector still uses cost model + fallback, but hints bias selection to minimize dequant transitions across adjacent heads and time slices.

4) Telemetry feedback loop: emit lightweight counters for dequant call frequency, average dequant size, headwise latency delta between INT8/FP8 kernels, and tail latency percentiles. A small analyzer task (offlined for phase 1) will suggest initial hint weights per model and per route.

Tradeoffs and decisions:
- Aligning caches increases allocated memory slightly; we target <8% additional KV memory for typical sequences and will gate by a config per-deployment tier (on by default for hosted, opt-in for constrained Dedicated).
- Hints are advisory to avoid correctness regressions; the runtime must always be able to fall back to FP32 safe path if numeric mismatch is detected. We'll reuse existing fallback policies.
- Subword grouping increases request latency for very low-concurrency (<2 requests) but provides net throughput/latency benefits at typical PLG loads. We will measure and gate behind a heuristic that disables grouping when overall queue occupancy is < threshold.

Implementation notes:
- Add allocator flags and new metadata field on KVCache allocation objects (string-typed flag values to keep serialization simple).
- Extend microbatch joiner in the prefill scheduler with an extra grouping key derived from tokenizer metadata.
- Kernel-hint API: a tiny struct serialized as 3 short strings (precision, magnitude, hint_score) attached to the op descriptor. Keep footprint < 32 bytes per head to avoid scheduling overhead.

Compatibility:
- Default behavior: hints disabled and alignment off to preserve existing behavior. Deployment will start with internal runtime image "runtime-1.22-hintproto" for validation.
tasks: A: changes to KV allocator and allocation metadata + unit tests
B: prefill scheduler: subword-based microbatch grouping and heuristics
C: kernel-hint metadata plumbing and kernel selector integration
D: telemetry hooks and initial analyzer to produce hint suggestions
E: end-to-end perf test harness for decode and prefill with representative models
F: safety/fallback tests to ensure no accuracy regressions and deterministic FP32 fallback
G: docs: console flags, runtime config, and rollout runbook
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end decode p50 latency reduced by >=6% on the quant-friendly benchmark (gpt-like, seq_len=1024, batch=4) when alignment + hints are enabled and comparator kernels allowed.
2) Dequant call count per token reduced by >=40% in typical streaming workloads compared to baseline runtime-1.21
3) No >0.5% drop in model token-output quality metrics (per model smoke tests) when using hint-driven kernel selection vs baseline FP32 fallback
4) Rollout can be toggled per-route via runtime flag and observed metrics in console; monitoring dashboards surface dequant rate and hint hit ratio
5) Memory overhead for cache alignment must be <8% on tested sequences or feature toggled off automatically
